purpose: Content shapes to drive through the real vLLM 0.19.1 gemma4 tool parser, chosen so that each one isolates one character class that could break a delimiter-based format. Case p01 is the exact content from the run-2 failure, taken from the file the agent read, not invented.

provenance.p01_source: reference/compare_run2/pilot/B__rich_3278/traces/trace_rich_3278.json, read_file observation at step 4 (the real rich/ansi.py text)
provenance.recorded_outputs: reference/compare_run2_malformed_calls.json holds the parser's OUTPUT for the run-2 attempts. It is not a raw model completion and must not be described as one.
provenance.format_status: UNKNOWN until the parser source is read. Cases carry content only; the wire rendering is supplied by the harness from the parser's own expected format.

cases.shape: regex: backslashes, triple quotes, commas, colons
cases.question: does old_string survive?
baseline: does anything survive at all?
is a comma a pair separator?
is a colon a key/value separator?
the run-2 residue ended with a backtick: is a backtick a quote character here?
does escaping survive one round trip?
run-2 arrived double-escaped: does the parser or the model double it?
is a newline significant to the format?

cases.shape: non-ASCII, including the CJK brackets seen in the run-2 variant
cases.question: does Unicode survive, and can it appear where the model did not put it?
control: this is what a genuine missing parameter looks like, distinct from one lost in transit

cases.shape: content that literally contains the text 'old_string:'
cases.question: can content spell a parameter name and be split on it? this is the run-2 residue's signature
